segments.text: Every day, I'm on the phone with people suffering from frightening symptoms that began shortly after they were vaccinated, and many of them have nowhere else to turn.

segments.text: My name is Angela Wolbrecht.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: I've spent more than 25 years as a nurse, caring for women, infants and children, as well as patients in emergency medicine.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: I know what these patients are experiencing because it happened to me.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: In January 2021, I was eager to receive the COVID vaccine.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: I drove three hours to get it because I wanted to help end the pandemic and protect the people around me.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Within 12 minutes of receiving the shot, my body went numb.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: My heart was racing, my blood pressure reached a dangerously high level, and I was taken to the emergency room by ambulance.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: In the weeks that followed, I became so ill that I prepared a living trust and wrote letters to my daughter in case I didn't survive.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Thankfully, I received early and aggressive medical care and eventually recovered.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: But that frightening experience showed me how little help was available for people suffering from vaccine injuries.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Today, through the Vaccine Safety Research Foundation, I provide that help.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: One reason these patients struggle is that many doctors and nurses receive little training in recognizing vaccine injuries.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: I know this firsthand.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Before my own injury, I had worked in a hospital for 17 years and administered vaccines, yet I had never even been taught about theirs.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: When patients arrive with symptoms affecting multiple parts of the body, medical professionals may not recognize the pattern or know where to refer them.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Some patients are told that their symptoms are psychological and sent home without answers.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Through VSRF, I connect patients with physicians, participate in medical appointments, help document their injuries, and advocate for them when they're hospitalized.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: We never charge patients for my help.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Many of the people who contact me have been suffering for years.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Some have lost their jobs, their health insurance, and their savings.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Others have been left frightened and alone in emergency rooms, unable to get anyone to listen.

segments.text: I've spoken with patients while they were writing in ambulances.

segments.text: When I can be physically present, I can see what's happening, speak directly with the medical team, help the patient understand what is being proposed, and remain beside them during one of the most frightening experiences of their life.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: In one urgent case, a young woman's condition was rapidly deteriorating in the hospital.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: I advocated for her by phone, ordered the first flight I could get, and remained involved in her care for months.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Today, she and her family credit that intervention with helping to save her life.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
